status: proposed by judge; coordinator freezes into brief.qualityCriteria
style: Warm, softly lit cartoon 3D limestone (finish like inputs/warm-soft-reference.png, material like the target and issue-76 concept). Calm readable planes with subtle stone detail; no photoreal grit, no paint-over.
immutableTechnicalConstraints: Full piece set and ids unchanged: reef-00..15 x a,b,c plus reef-rubble-a, reef-rubble-b (50 pieces), one south view each.

Ground footprint equals collision shape: open faces inset 0.08 cell, faces against solid flush to the cell edge, exposed corners rounded radius 0.35 cell, other corners square. Chips/cracks bite inward <= 0.03 cell and never change the outline at ground level.
Slab layout per pattern unchanged; slab height 0.32 cell with per-slab variation within +/-12% as now.
Reef-facing cell edges meet flush with no seabed gap; interior grooves stay narrow.
Rubble under 0.1 cell high and inside its cell.
Camera, frame 768x2048 native / 384x1024 published, ground root, native scale 4, publish downsample (ffmpeg lanczos 2x) unchanged; R.configure + R.square_footing recipe.

Lighting stays in the recipe rig family: broad overhead plus eight symmetric fills, low blue world, no preferred horizontal direction, no cast shadow on the ground (transparent background stays clean).
Seam safety: surface detail is world/object-space procedural or per-slab, never dependent on a cell's mask.
Nothing grows on the reef (no coral, kelp, moss, shells).
Native procedural Blender output from an editable recipe; any raster texture must be stored inside the experiment and bound as a resource.
evidenceRequired: All 50 native captures (768x2048) and published sprites (384x1024) listed in packet.json with hashes.
independent-assembly assembly.png of the same 6x6 patch as inputs/original.png.

A seam stress sheet: at minimum horizontal and vertical pairs that join a cell to a neighbour of a different mask and different pattern (e.g. 02-a|08-b, 0A-c|0A-a style runs, 04 over 01, a full 3x3 of mask 15 with mixed patterns, and an open-edge corner piece beside a solid run), at native size and 2x.

validation.json: per-piece alpha footprint at the ground plane compared to the original captures (outline unchanged within tolerance), frame/root registration, rubble height, and confirmation that light objects/energies stay symmetric.
Renderer repeatability: re-render of one unchanged piece to set a pixel tolerance before judging numeric diffs.

color: Tops are warm cream-to-peach limestone, noticeably warmer than the original near-white (target direction approx RGB 245-255, 210-228, 160-185), with visible but gentle per-slab variation: a few slightly warmer/peachier, a few slightly paler or greyer. No slab is white, orange or grey enough to look like a different material.

Front (south) faces are a clearly deeper warm tan/ochre than tops (target direction approx RGB 170-195, 120-145, 75-100), darkening slightly toward the seabed. The top/front value step is obvious at phone size.
Whole patch remains unmistakably paler and warmer than the blue-navy bedrock and the seabed; no blue or green cast on the stone except a faint cool ambient in shadowed grooves.
Rubble uses the same palette as the slabs (lit top in top tone, sides in front tone).
shapeVolume: Each slab reads as a solid stone block with a lit top, a soft chamfer and a shaded front; the cell reads as one smashable mass, not a grid of tiles.
Approved silhouette, heights and rounded exposed corners are visibly identical to the original at ground level; small chipped corners on top edges read as stone wear, not as shape changes.
Grooves between slabs read as narrow warm shadow lines; no seabed blue visible inside a cell and no dark wedge where a lower slab peeks out.
lightingHighlights: Chamfered top edges carry a soft warm highlight (lighter than the top, same hue family), replacing the original's cool grey rim band.
Soft, even lighting with no directional bias: the same slab type looks the same whatever its position or mask; no cast shadows on the ground and no blown-out highlight patches.
Gentle top gradient or occlusion is allowed only if it is symmetric/position-independent so it cannot step across a seam.
materialDetail: Fine hairline cracks on a subset of slabs (roughly a third to a half), one or two per slab, slightly darker/paler than the top and thin enough to stay subtle at phone size; they may run over the chamfer and down the front.
Sparse small pores/pits on tops (a few per slab), not a uniform noise grain.
Front faces show 2-4 soft horizontal strata bands per slab height, slightly wavy, at heights driven by world/object Z so adjacent pieces line up.
Occasional small chipped corners/edge nicks on slab tops within the 0.03-cell tolerance; detail density consistent across all 48 cell pieces.
Overall detail stays in the warm-soft cartoon register: crisp calm planes first, texture second; no photo-noise, no high-frequency speckle.
artifactFreeReadability: At the published 384x1024 size and at about 360 px across the 6x6 assembly, the patch reads instantly as pale breakable limestone distinct from bedrock; cracks/strata visible as texture, nothing shimmering or speckled.

No triangulation/diagonal shading lines on tops, no black or near-black patches, no z-fighting/coplanar flicker, no exposed interior faces, no normal seams at bevels, no halos or fringes on the alpha edge against the seabed.
Rubble remains crisp small low fragments with clear top/side shading.
seamContinuity: Across every flush cell edge in the assembly and the seam stress sheet, top tone, front strata heights, chamfer treatment and light level do not jump; the seam is visible only as the normal narrow groove that also separates slabs within a cell.
Front strata of horizontally adjacent pieces in a row align in height and spacing.
No crack, chip or pore pattern is cut off with a hard straight edge at a cell boundary (cracks should stay within a slab or be world-continuous).
Open-edge (exposed) faces may differ only by geometry (inset/rounded corner), not by a different surface treatment.

priorityRanking: 1. Warm limestone colour/value structure: peach-cream tops over a clearly deeper warm tan front, gentle per-slab variation, still clearly pale vs bedrock.
2. Seamless joins across masks and patterns: no tone/light/strata jump at cell seams; strata aligned in Z.
3. Breakable stone cues readable at phone size: front strata plus hairline cracks and small chipped corners (sparse pores as 2x detail), consistent density.
4. Soft warm chamfer highlight and grooves as thin warm shadows (no grey plastic rim, no blue slivers, no dark wedges).
5. Artifact-free output with locked footprint/height/rubble unchanged and matching rubble material.
scoring: Comparative 1-10 per dimension (shapeVolume, color, lightingHighlights, materialDetail, artifactFreeReadability) against original (baseline) and target; seam continuity is a gating check reported in observations/blockers. No numeric pass mark; approval requires visible improvement toward the target, all locked constraints met with evidence, and no material defect in any required view.
conflictsNoted: Target chips that cut the silhouette or rounded corners conflict with the locked footprint tolerance; reproduce chips only on top edges within 0.03 cell.
Target's per-cell crack placement is not seam-aware; native cracks must not depend on mask.
